html:
The American war in Vietnam began in earnest after the Gulf of Tonkin incident of August 1964, a naval clash off North Vietnam, and lasted until the last US combat troops left in March 1973.

On 2 August 1964 North Vietnamese boats fought the destroyer USS Maddox; a second attack reported two days later almost certainly never happened. Congress passed a resolution letting President Johnson wage war. US Marines landed at Da Nang in March 1965, and by 1969 over half a million Americans were in South Vietnam, while US planes bombed the North and the Ho Chi Minh Trail.

The Tet Offensive of 1968 turned American opinion. The Vietnam War went on after the US left, until the fall of Saigon in 1975. Millions of Vietnamese died, along with about 58,000 Americans, and the land was poisoned by Agent Orange.
sum: The American war in Vietnam began in earnest after the Gulf of Tonkin incident of August 1964, a naval clash off North Vietnam, and lasted until the last US combat troops left in March 1973.
